summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent lower extremity cellulitis, chronic ulcers, and multiple comorbidities was admitted for worsening cellulitis around a left ankle ulcer, with copious drainage and spreading erythema. She had recently failed to complete a prior course of IV vancomycin due to PICC line dislodgement. IV vancomycin was restarted, and a new PICC line was placed on hospital day 3 with confirmed appropriate positioning on chest imaging. The infection showed clinical improvement during the admission, with reduced redness, swelling, and drainage. The right ankle was monitored for possible early cellulitis but remained stable. She was discharged home with home health services to complete antibiotic therapy and wound care, with follow-up planned with dermatology and her gerontologist.
